subject: Dedicated pilot follow-up — Baycrest performance validation & next steps
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>

Cc: Alex Cho <alex@baycrest.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pilot follow-up — Baycrest performance validation & next steps

Hi Samir / Alex,

Thanks again for taking the time today — good discussion. Quick recap and a concrete pilot plan so we can move to validation quickly. I’ve attached the sample prompts and a brief pilot requirements doc.

Recap (from call)
- Workload: mixed chat + short instruction completions (avg prompt ~45 tokens, typical replies 35–120 tokens).
- Target SLOs: p95 latency <= 220ms for short-turn streaming (single-turn chat, 1–2 tokens/sec streaming acceptable), p99 <= 450ms for heavier completions; sustained throughput target ~120 reqs/sec with 80 concurrent streaming sessions.
- Quality constraint: must match current baseline 0.92 Rouge-L on our proprietary prompt set; we’ll record outputs and run a blinded eval.

Pilot proposal (what Redwood will deliver)
1) Validation matrix across GPU variants: H100-80GB (FP16 & int8), A100-40GB (FP16 & int8), and L4/Inferentia-style cost-focused quantized variant.
2) Reserved pool sizing options: small (4xH100), medium (8xA100), and cost-optimized (12xL4-equivalent). We’ll run both peak-sustained and burst scenarios.
3) Tests: streaming latency (prefix warm, cold start), sustained throughput for 60m window, concurrency ramp to 100 sessions, KV cache hit simulation using representative prefix set.
4) Observable outputs: token-level latency, GPU util, tail-latency heatmap, cost-per-1k-tokens estimate, and per-prompt quality diffs.

Asks from Baycrest
- Confirm the SLO targets above (p95/p99) or propose edits.
- Provide the redacted sample prompt CSV (I attached a template; please replace PII).
- Approve a 2-week pilot window (we estimate 5 business days of active benchmarking + 3 days analysis/reporting).

Next steps / timeline
- You confirm SLOs + send prompts by EOD Friday 5/5.
- Redwood schedules infra and shares a short benchmark plan by 5/8.
- Kickoff call and access exchange week of 5/13; active bench 5/15–5/19; delivery of results 5/22.

Attachments: baycrest-sample-prompts.csv (template), pilot-requirements.docx.

If that all looks good I’ll loop in Infra to reserve the candidate pools and Karthik will lead the tech run.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0183

We’ll attach the sanitized prompts later today (using your template). Also attaching a short traffic trace (see quoted attach). Could you add a short note on how Redwood simulates cold start vs warm KV-cache in the pilot?

Subject: RE: Dedicated pilot follow-up — Baycrest performance validation & next steps

Priya / Ben — digesting the ask and initial numbers. High-level tech notes and proposed validation plan below. Putting down concrete action items so we don’t drift.

Tech notes (summary)
- H100 (80GB) will give best single-request latency due to larger memory and better fp16 kernels for long KV caches. Expect ~15–25% lower tail latency vs A100 for streaming workloads at similar concurrency.
- A100 (40GB) wins on price per GPU for sustained throughput if you can sharded model across more nodes; expect ~10–20% higher p95 vs H100 but similar p99 when using tuned batching.
- L4-equivalent quantized fleet is cost-effective (~40–55% lower $/1k tokens) but may require int8 calibration and re-eval on quality. For Baycrest’s 0.92 Rouge-L target we’ll need a small quality delta check.

Pilot matrix (what we will run)
- Config A (latency-focused): 4xH100, small batch sizes, continuous streaming mode, KV cache enabled; tests: 1) cold-start 50x cold requests; 2) warm-run 60m at 80 concurrent streaming sessions; 3) tail-latency percentile capture.
- Config B (balanced): 8xA100, tuned batching windows, KV tiering (local+shared); tests: sustained 120 reqs/sec for 60m, burst ramp 0->200 reqs/sec in 120s, concurrency ramp to 120.
- Config C (cost-optimized): L4-equivalent nodes in quantized int8, validate quality on blind eval set, run 2x sustained windows to measure drift.

How we simulate cold vs warm KV cache
- Cold: restart model servers + flush in-memory KV caches; run 50 isolated cold requests spaced 30s apart.
- Warm: preload KV prefixes derived from your traffic trace; run continuous streaming sessions to warm caches and then measure.

Action items (owners and ETA)
- Ben: prepare benchmark harness + perf dashboard templates; provisionable infra config (5/8).
- Priya: confirm SLO wording and own scheduling with Baycrest; confirm pilot agreement execution (5/5).
- Karthik: finalize GPU mix and nominal resource sizing; produce cost delta summary for 4xH100 vs 8xA100 vs L4 (5/7).

I’ll draft the test scripts and stress scenarios; Ben will wire up Grafana dashboards for the trial.

-Karthik
